title: Capacity Rebalance Decision Matrix and Minimal Viable Scope (MVS) Experiment Plan for Cycle 2026-W08
creator: Avery Chen
description: Context: Ahead of the upcoming cycle we need a repeatable, low-friction decision process for rebalancing staff and trimming scope when we hit surges or unexpected platform incidents. This ticket captures a decision matrix, an MVS experiment plan to validate minimal scope cuts against customer impact, and the runbook for communicating changes to stakeholders. Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-decision for scope cuts to <48 hours; 2) Protect highest-value SLAs and customer-facing flows; 3) Validate that small, targeted scope trims materially reduce peak load without significant regression in user metrics. Out of scope: hiring, long-term staffing changes, permanent roadmap re-prioritization (this is a cycle-level operational playbook).
comments: 2026-02-17 - Avery Chen: Drafted initial decision matrix and shared with Eng leads. Core heuristic: preserve SLO-critical work, defer non-blocking UX polish, and convert low-priority API additions into post-cycle backlog. Link to spreadsheet with weighted impact model included.

2026-02-20 - Eng lead (Jon Morales): Flagged two constraints: (1) Dedicated autoscaler work depends on infra spike fixes (ENG-4092); (2) Redis KV cache optimization will free ~12% capacity but requires 2 days of focused work. Recommended we treat that optimization as a short runway item in the matrix rather than a scope cut.

2026-02-23 - Design (Priya Singh): Provided a short list of degrade-safe UI elements we can hide without breaking flows. Suggested A/B style rollout for user-visible changes as part of the MVS experiment.

2026-02-28 - PM sync: Agreed on decision tiers (Tier 0: emergency SLO protection; Tier 1: aggressive scope freeze and MVS experiments; Tier 2: optional deferrals). Owner assignments for each tier documented in runbook.

2026-03-03 - Maya Patel: Added experiment plan to validate two candidate scope cuts: 'defer analytics dashboard refresh' and 'disable non-essential model variants for low-tier customers'. KPIs: error rate, median latency, token cost per request, trial-conversion lift/drop. Dashboard queries and alert thresholds outlined.

2026-03-08 - Solutions Eng (Diego Alvarez): Built a smoke-config in staging to toggle model variants and analytics refresh; created feature flags and a small traffic split for canary. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2281 referenced.

2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Decision matrix finalized. Next steps: run two 48-hour MVS experiments during 2026-W08, observe infra metrics and customer-facing KPIs, and reconvene for go/no-go on scope trims. Notify Sales/Support via the runbook channel before experiments begin.
